searchText: I have a couple of questions regarding decentralized trading. I asked on reddit and a couple of Discord channels and didn't get any answers. 1) is there some platform like uniswap but where one is allowed to submit a limit bid order, say to exchange N tokens X for M tokens Y, one deposits the tokens X into an audited contract until a matching order appears or until the order is cancelled. It seems to me that contract technology is capable of this and that there should be demand for this so I presume this exists. 2) similar questions for options: I hold N token X and want to sell a call option at with strike M tokens Y for price L tokens Z. I deposit my tokens X into a contract and if someone wants to buy he deposits the tokens Z. The contract then a) gives me L tokens Z, b) mints N new tokens OptionX and gives it to the buyer. If the buyer wants to execute it deposits back the tokens along with the tokens Y, then the contract gives him my tokens X, i receive Y and option X is burned. I haven't seen any of this, but I'm very new to Ethereum and have never traded (nor am I interested, in any case I'd be more interested in implementing this) What you have described is possible, though the latter requires an oracle which has some security issues that you have to consider. Maybe I'm looking in wrong spots or with wrong terms Search Twitter The term MEV can be misleading as one would assume it is miners who are extracting this value. In reality, the MEV present on Ethereum today is predominantly captured by DeFi traders through structural arbitrage trading strategies; miners indirectly profit from these traders’ transaction fees. One example of such structural arbitrage opportunities are Uniswap price arbitrage trades: when a Uniswap pool’s assets become mispriced, a profit opportunity is created to arbitrage the Uniswap pool back to parity with other trading venues. Of course, rather than letting the trader pay them a transaction fee for the privilege of collecting the arb profit, a miner could simply decide to run this strategy themselves. Ah, the devil's playground Wait actually devil just got banned from twitter Mev refers more to the miner seeing this transaction in the mempool. Computing the transactions needed to front run for maximum alpha and then constructing a block and submit those perfectly timed txns for the lowest possible gwei, thus letting the trader do all the work and you extract all the value.
